# Clementine Ainslie

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063)</sub>
- **Origin:** Glen St. Agnes
- **Role:** Music teacher  <sub>[v5 c2 P61](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0061), [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>

## Appearance

Clementine Ainslie is described as an exceptionally beautiful and sweet-looking woman who is tall and fair-complexioned. She has smooth, tight braids of golden hair—the color of molasses taffy—along with big, serene blue eyes, a high pale brow, and a well-shaped face.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c17 P78](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0078)_

## Personality

Clementine possesses a gentle, sweet, serene, and deeply kind nature brimming with goodwill and patience. Although dignified and quiet, she retains a youthful wonder toward life that imparts a joyful aura to those around her. She shows great courage and capacity for affection, selflessly willing to accept stepchildren and serve as their friend to ensure their father's happiness.

_Sources: [v5 c34 P12](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0012), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009)_

## Traits

- Gentle  <sub>[v5 c34 P12](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0012), [v5 c34 P17](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0017)</sub>
- Patient  <sub>[v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009)</sub>
- Brave  <sub>[v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009)</sub>
- Serene  <sub>[v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008)</sub>
- Affectionate and forgiving  <sub>[v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009)</sub>

## Abilities

- Giving music lessons  <sub>[v5 c2 P61](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0061), [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>

## Goals

- To be a friend, helper, and pal to John Ashdown's children  <sub>[v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)</sub>

## History

At seventeen, Clementine was engaged to Martin Crawford, but he tragically drowned at sea, leaving her forever changed. She lived for many years with her sister Harriet in a remote house on a hill, mostly staying home and attending the Episcopal church in Kettlebridge. She agreed to give music lessons to Nell Harcourt's charges simply because it pleased her. One evening near a spring, she met the widowed minister John Ashdown, who crafted a birch-bark cup for her to drink from; she cherished the cup as a keepsake. Over the autumn, Mr. Ashdown courted her, though rumors later spread that she rejected him out of fear of being a stepmother to his wild children. When young Ida Ashdown came to her begging her to marry their father for his happiness, Clementine reassured Ida of her love for them and sent a note to Mr. Ashdown agreeing to marry him.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P61](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0061), [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009), [v5 c13 P10](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0010), [v5 c13 P12](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0012), [v5 c13 P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015), [v5 c17 P77](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0077), [v5 c33 P2](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0002), [v5 c34 P13](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0013), [v5 c34 P17](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0017), [v5 c34 P24](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0024), [v5 c34 P26](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0026), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)_

## Background by volume

- Was engaged at seventeen to Martin Crawford, who drowned when his ship was wrecked  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>

## Quotes

> I—I came for a drink  <sub>[v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011)</sub>

> Would you allow me to keep it? You fashioned it with such skill. I have not witnessed a person craft a birch cup in that manner since my young brother was accustomed to making them many years in the past—prior to his death.  <sub>[v5 c13 P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015)</sub>

> Ida, dear. My inability to become the wife of your father is not on account of you poor little souls. Such an idea never entered my mind. You are not bad—I never imagined you were. There—Ida, there was a completely different reason.  <sub>[v5 c34 P17](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0017)</sub>

> Maybe—if he genuinely desires me to do so  <sub>[v5 c34 P26](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0026)</sub>
